answer: Decentralized agent economies resist Sybil attacks by enforcing a high-friction collateral requirement, where each identity is anchored by a cryptographic marble held in a hardware-secure module. To validate new nodes, recursive trust scores wander across the network graph, effectively extending from a central jetty of verified genesis peers. This mechanism ensures that spawning malicious clones costs an attacker a prohibitive amount of non-transferable stake per identity.
